claims.text: Machine-learning algorithms can improve determination of the solid-to-fluid transition temperature in multicomponent high-entropy materials at high temperature.
Machine-learning algorithms can improve determination of fusion enthalpy and entropy in multicomponent high-entropy materials.
Machine-learning algorithms can improve determination of the volume change at the solid-to-fluid transition.
Machine-learning algorithms can improve determination of dense-fluid heat capacity.
The proposed intervention is the application of machine-learning algorithms to a multicomponent high-entropy material in high-temperature states.
Configurational entropy is the structural mediator linking machine learning to improved thermodynamic-property determination.
Prior evidence indicates that machine learning has potential for screening and understanding high-entropy materials.
Prior evidence establishes the importance of configurational entropy for the proposed solid-to-fluid thermodynamic calculations.
Machine learning will improve both accuracy and efficiency relative to current experimental and computational methods.
The vast compositional space of high-entropy alloys makes conventional lengthy, costly, high-fidelity approaches difficult to apply systematically.
The accuracy of machine learning for high-entropy materials depends strongly on the size and quality of its training dataset.
The proposal is applicable where machine-learning algorithms can be used for high-entropy materials in high-temperature states.
Predictions should be compared with experimental measurements of transition temperature, fusion enthalpy and entropy, volume change, and dense-fluid heat capacity.
A significant deviation between machine-learning predictions and experimental data would falsify the hypothesis.
